steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Blaze, what do you think of this one?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Mm... not bad!

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: What I mean is, do these tangerine cakes taste like the ones you remember?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Umm... well... not exactly.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: They're still not as sweet as the ones I had before. They also don't have quite the same mouth feel.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: That's strange. This place uses traditional cooking methods. Their snacks are definitely authentic. They haven't changed their recipes in one hundred years.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: One hundred years? Have tangerine cakes even been around that long?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: No, tangerine cakes are not quite that old, but many famous Baizao snacks do have quite a long history.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: The tangerine cake you are looking for were actually invented by a scholar who came to Baizao to study in its early years.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: The scholar's hometown was famous for its tangerines. After he moved to Baizao, he missed those tangerines. It was too far to go home and get them, so he improvised.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: He smashed up some old, dried tangerine peels and made them into dough, added some sugar, shortening, and spices, and baked them. It was a cheap, easy way to get his tangerine fix.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: He gave the recipe to his landlord in lieu of paying rent. He even wrote a small poem about them, 'These tangerine cakes are bright and fresh, just like the orange groves back home.'

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: After the scholar passed the imperial examination and assumed office, the tangerine cakes became very famous. People began to view them as a symbol of homesickness.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Interesting...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Symbolic food. First time I've ever heard something like that.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Yan is a vast land, with many different climate zones, each with their own cash crops and produce. That's why there are many different types of Yanese cuisine. You can trace all of Yan's history through its food.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: For example, Yan's Four Major Cuisines match up with its Four Great Restaurants, which predate Baizao's transformation into a nomadic city.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Cities develop, but flavors remain. It would be odd to find any snack without its own bit of history behind it.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: One of my colleagues told me that there are many different kinds of Tianshis in Yan. You know so much about food, you must be some kind of Tasty Food Tianshi, right?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: If there really was such an individual, someone who could use Arts to transform stones into vegetables, that might be worth studying, eh?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Alas, I am just an amateur foodie. I like to take notes on the food I eat, and its history. Over the years, I've compiled several notebooks full of such information.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: To put it another way, Blaze, if there really were a better recipe for tangerine cakes out there, surely someone here would know about it.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: But I'm telling you! The ones I had when I was younger, they were sweeter, and just better!

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: That really is rather odd...

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Traditional tangerine cakes emphasize the fresh essence of the tangerines, not the taste of their pulp. Very little sugar is used, because tangerine cakes are supposed to be a light snack.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: You're telling me you've eaten much sweeter tangerine cakes, and I'm telling you that I've never heard of such a thing.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Maybe we can ask one of the chefs around here to try cooking up a batch with extra sugar, so you can compare?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: But even if we do that, it doesn't prove that the sweeter variety of tangerine cakes ever actually existed before.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: What I want to know is, how did the taste of these tangerine cakes change during their journey from Baizao to Victoria. I'm sure there's a story there somewhere.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: It seems you're just as much of a foodie as I am.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: I was afraid you'd get tired of traipsing off to all these restaurants.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You're the guide. You lead, I follow.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Alright then. Let's keep looking!

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: My word, look at the time! We should have lunch first.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Hmm? Lunch?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Yes. It's lunchtime. Shouldn't we have some lunch?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: But I just finished eating snacks from five different restaurants!

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Snacks are snacks, but lunch is lunch. You must have a proper lunch, you know!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I don't think my tummy has any more room for lunch...

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Haha. I know one restaurant that I can guarantee won't make your tummy ache.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Will you give it a try?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You're the foodie here, so I, and my stomach, trust you!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: What's wrong?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I feel like... we're being followed.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: You... you're... an Imperial Guard?

steps.name: Imposing Woman
steps.text: No, no, no. Without darksteel armor, I'm not a proper member of the Imperial Guards. Officially, I'm a captain serving with the Yulin Guards.

steps.name: Imposing Woman
steps.text: Deputy Minister Lin, I doubt you'd want to encounter anyone wearing darksteel armor anyway, certainly not in broad daylight.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I once heard Taihe mention that there is a 'junior drillmaster' serving in the ranks the Imperial Guard apprentices. She's very young, but skilled beyond her years.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: That must be you. You're the junior drillmaster.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Hmph. I guess Taihe's still sore that I beat him in a couple matches last month. There's no need for name calling, though.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: No matter. I'd like to ask you, what are you doing here?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I'm investigating a case.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Does that case have anything to do with the former Minister of Rites? Has the Judicial Review Office issued you a search warrant?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: You're just a drillmaster. You have no authority to question whatever warrants I may or may not have, do you?

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: You have no authority to question my authority. Just answer my questions, please.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: ...Very well.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: I heard you were on a long business trip just recently. You left Baizao for a while, did you not?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: That's right. I went to go question a witness in an old case and update the case files.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: What old case? From when? What witness? Why are you just investigating it now?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I don't understand your line of questioning.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: If the Yulin Guards want to investigate the Judicial Review Office, I'll go submit the necessary documentation immediately.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: If that still isn't enough for you, I can have the Minister of the Judicial Review Office report to the Yulin Guards for questioning.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: My questions have nothing to do with the Judicial Review Office. They only concern you, Deputy Minister Lin.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: So you went to investigate an old case. What did you learn?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: ...Too much time has passed, so the trail has gone cold. I didn't learn anything.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Nothing? Really? Are you sure?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Nothing.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Alright. I believe you. However, remember that you are speaking to the Yulin Guards here. Your answers carry great weight.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Very good. I'm done discussing official business for now.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: So you still have some personal business you wish to discuss?

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Taihe, that dumb Forte, told me he doesn't have many friends in government. Well, you now count as one.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Well, I must warn you, don't stick your neck out too far.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Your worries are unfounded. I'm just pursuing the truth here, as it is my job to do. I'm not putting myself at any additional risk.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: ...Very good.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Give Taihe my regards.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: They are questioning why I'm here. Well, why are the Yulin Guards here?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Their presence here, I think, is proof that I'm on the right track.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Phew—

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Boy, am I stuffed. I never would have guessed that a roadside stand could make such amazing wontons. They're certainly better than the ones in the Rhodes Island cafeteria freezer!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I'm so stuffed that I want to just take a nap right here. Ah... nng...

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: After eating all that greasy street food, a nice, hearty bowl of wontons is the perfect thing to settle your stomach.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: The famous restaurants need no introduction. As your guide in Baizao, I figured I'd share some of my favorite lesser-known food spots.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Well I'm lucky to have found such a good tour guide. Thank you!

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Well, I'm also glad to have found a culinary companion. I tend to eat alone, which means I can only order one or two entrees for myself.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You know what they say, 'the more the merrier.' Now that I'm here, you can order as much food as you want.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Speaking of food, what is in these wontons, anyway? They're fantastic!

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Just meat and celery. The key ingredient is the soup!

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Most places use shellbeast caviar in wonton soup to enhance the flavor. Unfortunately, the finniness of the caviar crowds out the other flavors.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: This place uses soybean sprouts instead. This makes for a milder soup, which allows the flavor of the wontons to shine!

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: The meat filling for the wontons is fresh beast belly. After the wontons are cooked, the bits of fat will naturally seep into the soup.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: These wontons are light, yet delicious. They are made of high-quality ingredients which are hard to find elsewhere.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Well, do these wontons have a history? Do tell.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Not really. I just really like this particular wonton shop, I guess.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: When I get writer's block, or need a little pick-me-up, I come here and eat a bowl of wontons.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: The shopkeeper has been making wontons her whole life. She used to own this shop together with her husband.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Her husband fell ill and passed away, leaving her to raise her child alone. Later, her son joined the army, but he died in a Catastrophe up north several years ago.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: She's still running the place all by herself. She says she wants to continue the family legacy and preserve their authentic taste.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: What a sad story.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: There are many such sad stories. There is no joy without pain.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Over the years, as I've been coming to this shop, I've helped the lady with an errand or two. In return, she told me her family's secret recipe. She hopes that one day, after she's gone, I can pass on her craft to the next generation.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: I have something I want to ask you.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Are you really going through all this trouble with the tangerine cakes just because you made a bet with the Young Chef?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Why do you ask?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: I simply noticed that you weren't terribly focused on the taste of the delicacies at all. It seemed like you had some other purpose in mind.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Was it that obvious? Wow...

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: When you watch people eat, you see into their souls.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Sorry, I was just curious. If I've intruded on your privacy, I sincerely apologize.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Hey now! We're friends! I'm not keeping secrets from you.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You're right. I'm not really that concerned about the bet.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Those tangerine cakes, well, my father used to send them to me when he was living in Baizao.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Your father, was he Yanese?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Err... meh, whatever. I don't have anything to hide from you.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I grew up in Victoria, and my father is Yanese. One year, he suddenly returned to Yan for some reason.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I never saw him again, and he died over a decade later in a land foreign to me.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: I'm sorry, Blaze...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: It's not your fault. Why do you keep apologizing?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I didn't think much about it at first, but yesterday when you mentioned that sweet tangerine cakes are unusual, I thought, 'someone who knows how to make those cakes might have also known my dad.'

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Your dad… was also…

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: He was also what?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Oh... nothing...

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Well, I promise you that I will do everything in my power to help you find out the truth about your father—

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You're such a contradiction—so bold when you eat, yet so refined when you speak.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: When we're eating together, it's all good fun; we're good friends. Why do you turn into a different person as soon as you put down your chopsticks?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Friends?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: And another thing, why are you helping me look for these tangerine cakes in the first place?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Well, I'm writing a book.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Most cookbooks today only contain recipes from renowned chefs, yet the streets and the countryside are full of unique delicacies that few people ever pay heed.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: I hope to collect all these recipes into a book. Perhaps, years later, people will read this book and learn of Baizao's unique cuisine. Hm... it's just a silly dream of mine, is all.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: And also...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: I think I'll keep that a secret for now.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Well, as long as we're out here, you might as well take me to a few more places, yeah?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Sure! Where do you want to go?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Let me see... this letter mentions the Virtue Bookstore, the Humble Garden, and the Baizao Academy.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Hey... what does this word mean?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Can you let me have a look?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: This is a letter? Why is it so greasy?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I didn't do that! It was like that when I opened it! I don't know what my dad was doing when he wrote it.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: So these are all letters that your father wrote to you?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Yes. The few that I managed to save.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: (Strange, this stationery... it's...)

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Hmm? What is it?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: N-Nothing. It's just that most of the places mentioned in this letter no longer exist.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Huh? But it was only written a decade ago.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: For Baizao, a decade is enough for the whole city to change.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Have you noticed that anything has changed since arriving in Baizao?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Well, aside from the food, there are all these energy poles all over the place. It seems like kind of a waste.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: It may seem wasteful, but in fact, we have no other choice.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: The city of Baizao was founded a long, long time ago.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: At that time, Yan had just experienced a great war, and the country was in dire straits. However, suddenly, an extremely rich Originium vein was discovered right next to the ruins of a battlefield.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Wow. What impeccable timing! You Yanese sure are lucky!

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: No. It wasn't lucky at all. The Originium vein was rich... too rich. It attracted too many Originium particles in one place, which eventually led to Catastrophe.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Basically, not only was it difficult to mine, but it also created a vast stretch of land that was prone to Catastrophes, and there was nothing the Yanese could do about it.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: That is, until one of the Tianshis had an idea—they could build a city right on top of the Originium vein. The city infrastructure would deplete the excess Originium energy, preventing further Catastrophes.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Building a city on top of an Originium mine? That sounds like a recipe for disaster!

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: It was indeed an extremely dangerous undertaking. However, the True Lung decided to go ahead with it... and that's how Baizao was founded.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: How did they do it? I can't even imagine...

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Honestly, I'm not totally sure either. In all the Yanese history books, there is only a single passage that talks about that period—

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: 'Skilled individuals were sent to the disaster zone, and after fifty-three years of effort, a city was built and established as the capital. The city was named Baizao, with the hope of tending all cooking stoves under heaven.'

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: As for the more advanced technical details, you'd probably have to look at some of the materials from the Tianshi Bureaus. That's beyond my area of expertise.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: So to this day, the Baizao government still encourages us to use this energy.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Baizao is constantly changing. That's how these skyscrapers appeared, as well as the numerous nomadic city plates.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: And what happened to the people who built the city?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I'm completely stuffed, but I still haven't found the taste I'm looking for.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: I've taken you to every restaurant I know that sells such cakes.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Maybe tomorrow we can go look in some of the larger restaurants.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: *burp*

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: What did I tell you? What did I tell you?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: You looked the whole day, yet you couldn't find your so-called, 'authentic tangerine cakes', could you?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: You were following us all day?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You were afraid we would find better food, weren't you?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Me? Afraid? Pah!

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: I already told you before, if you're looking for the best chef in Baizao, you've already found him. If I can't cook it, no one else can.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Blaze, I've tasted his food. It really is quite excellent. A rare treat.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: You really know how to flatter!

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Besides, you're arguing over the details in how a single pastry is made—how could that possibly be the standard for judging a chef's skill?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Still, I can see that you, chef, are still curious about these sweet tangerine cakes that Blaze is talking about, are you not?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: ....Not really.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: How about this? You two set aside your bet, and we'll see where we can find these sweet tangerine cakes.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: That way, Blaze will find the tangerine cakes she's looking for, and you, chef, will learn a new recipe. Sounds like a delightful arrangement, no?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Huh? What?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: What about my one month of free meals?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Hmph, my cooking skills are so superb that no one can match them, but there are other chefs that I respect. If I had to name one in particular, it would be...

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Well... it would be...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Who?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: The head chef of Ding Feng Lou, the highest rated of the Four Great Restaurants.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: You mean, Mr. Mo Bufu?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Everyone at Ding Feng Lou is busy preparing for the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies. That means the old man is prepping for his last feast.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: His last feast? You mean, he's retiring?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Who knows! That old man's been challenging people left and right lately—really showing off...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: What are you waiting for? Let's go!

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: It's not so simple...

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Chef Mo is quite an important man. He is responsible for the entire feast. We can't bother him with trifling matters such as some tangerine cakes.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: The girl is clever, but she's only half right. If you really do want to go meet him, I have a way.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Last month's receipts?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: No. Not in this pocket...

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Ah. Here it is.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: An invitation to the Ding Feng Lou Chef Selection...

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Blaze, we won't get many opportunities to meet Chef Mo.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Then what are we waiting for? Whoever is going to the competition, take me with you!

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: As to who will participate in the competition...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Huh? What are you looking at me for?
